inspection_summary: Audited all 1,572 logical lines of this preliminary collaborative RH reference. The usable material forms a broad semantic map: definitions and representations of L-functions, hierarchies and weakenings of RH, translations between zeros and arithmetic error terms, positivity/completeness/deformation/matrix criteria, spectral and operator-algebraic analogies, and two explicitly defeated sufficient-condition programs. Forty material units are retained, including both immutable v1 IDs; one v1 span needs bounded surrounding context. Empty subsections, repeated examples, page furniture, and two formula-damaged criteria are dispositioned without being promoted.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the functional-equation, Euler-product, completed-function, critical-strip, and zero-counting representations used throughout the source.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter A.4: analogues of zeta-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates periodic-orbit spectral determinants to dynamical zeta functions and zero spectra.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter B: Riemann hypotheses and perspectives
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates RH variants and weaker zero-distribution hypotheses, then motivates arithmetic and spectral perspectives.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter C introduction through Farey and cyclotomic criteria
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Maps RH to prime errors, cancellation of arithmetic functions, extremal inequalities, Farey discrepancy, and cyclotomic height.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the explicit formula, coefficient positivity, derivative zero location, and logarithmic-derivative positivity to re-express RH.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Collects density/completeness, mollification, series-growth, Fourier positivity, heat deformation, Hankel determinant, and divisibility-matrix criteria.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents the Bost-Connes phase-transition construction and records two sufficient-condition approaches whose hoped-for hypotheses fail.

accepted_units.title: Completed L-functions share reflection symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares zeta, Dirichlet, Dedekind, modular, Maass, and higher-rank completions, exposing the common move of adjoining archimedean factors before reflecting s to 1-s.

accepted_units.why_material: It gives the reusable local-to-global representation across several L-function families and identifies higher-rank degree through local factors.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; the local-factor pattern is recoverable, while the newform bad-prime notation at 211-215 should be checked against the scan before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Completion and recentering turn symmetry into evenness and real critical-line data
accepted_units.why_material: Completing zeta removes its pole, recentering gives an even Xi function, and the Hardy Z representation converts critical-line values into a real-valued function without changing their modulus.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is self-contained after the functional-equation family has been introduced.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive but conceptually recoverable; the OCR of the phase factor at 246-253 is imperfect and exact reuse needs scan verification.

accepted_units.why_material: The source derives the basic zero geometry by combining a zero-free Euler-product half-plane with functional-equation reflection, then distinguishes trivial gamma-factor zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Depends conceptually on the preceding Euler-product and completion units, not on omitted outside text.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-led; line 262 is syntactically damaged, but the half-plane/strip decomposition remains explicit in 258-266.

accepted_units.why_material: N(T), N0(T), and N(sigma,T) encode distinct strengths of zero information and turn RH, partial on-line results, and density questions into comparable counting statements.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument-principle estimate and multiplicity discussion at 286-301 provide material interpretation for the counting notation.

accepted_units.title: Square-root cancellation in prime-weighted and Möbius sums encodes RH

accepted_units.title: A heat-like deformation turns RH into the sign of a real-zero threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The one-parameter family has only real zeros above a threshold Lambda, so RH becomes the boundary statement Lambda <= 0 and Newman's conjecture locates it at criticality.

accepted_units.title: Positivity of all Hankel-type determinants characterizes RH

accepted_units.why_material: The source defines KMS equilibrium, symmetry, and spontaneous breaking, then poses and states solutions of zeta and Dedekind-zeta dynamical-system realization problems.

accepted_units.why_material: The exact sequence, strong-approximation quotient, finite solution fibers, and averaging endomorphisms construct the algebraic input for the crossed product.

accepted_units.why_material: The universal covariant representation and semigroup crossed product are followed by a splitting that restricts the semigroup and recovers the stated Bost-Connes algebra and outer symmetry group.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Reflection symmetry to real-zero geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Completion and recentering systematically convert functional equations into critical-line or real-zero formulations whose scope varies with the chosen L-function family.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a representational synthesis, not evidence that the zeros satisfy the desired geometry.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local-global axioms to quantitative zero questions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Euler factors and coefficient orthogonality motivate an axiomatic class in which zero-free, density, and prime-number-theorem questions can be asked uniformly.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several bridges are conjectural in the source, and the Selberg-class identification problem remains open there.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-zero translation pipeline
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Logarithmic derivatives, Tauberian arguments, summatory cancellation, and explicit formulas provide multiple interfaces translating zero location into arithmetic error or positivity statements.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The criteria have different hypotheses and levels of quantitative strength; this synthesis does not make them interchangeable proofs.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral realization constraints
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Spectral determinants, CUE statistics, periodic-orbit analogies, and partition-function phase transitions jointly constrain what a zeta-related dynamical or operator model might need to reproduce.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source supplies analogies and constructions with different outputs, not one operator whose spectrum proves RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positivity, approximation, and matrix certificates
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A wide family of RH equivalences replaces direct zero location by positivity, density, approximation error, or determinant tests over increasingly rich witnesses.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Equivalence alone does not identify a tractable witness or algorithm, and several displayed formulas need scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Deformation and finite-matrix encodings
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Heat deformation, moment matrices, and divisibility matrices recast RH as a threshold or asymptotic hierarchy that can be probed away from direct zero enumeration.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not establish that these encodings simplify the underlying difficulty.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Approximation criteria versus failed approximants
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Dirichlet polynomials appear both in a successful weighted approximation equivalence and in a zero-free partial-sum strategy defeated by unavoidable zeros, illustrating that the chosen functional and topology determine whether an approximant route is viable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The two polynomial families and conditions are distinct; the contrast is diagnostic rather than a logical implication between the results.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for this normalized source: every substantive subsection or coherent mathematical mechanism is either represented by an accepted unit (including both carried v1 units), retained as supporting context, or explicitly dispositioned as repetitive example material, an empty placeholder, page/reference furniture, or extraction-defective mathematics. Further splitting would mainly isolate formulas from their setup, duplicate already represented criteria, or promote unsafe OCR.
stop_reason: The audit reached line 1,572 after accounting for the full preliminary resource. The final source region contains one fully represented failure catalogue followed only by empty Zeta Gallery and Anecdotes headings; elsewhere the only unselected mathematical-looking passages are repeated modular examples, stubs promised for later expansion, and the unrecoverable Volchkov and truncated Hardy-Littlewood formulas. Thus no unaccounted usable mechanism remains.
